title: Late-Claim Percent on Member Appeals to Out-of-Network Plans Paying First — Insurance Coverage & Claims
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims — member appeals to an out-of-network plan that pays first.** The first-plan member appeal's late-claim percent follows the calendar days from the order's collection date, as shown on the patient's order under **Laboratory Test Orders**, to the claim's filing date. The order is the order the appealed claim bills.

The late-claim percent is the first-plan far late percent of **85** where those days exceed the first-plan far late days of **90**; the first-plan near late percent of **95** where they exceed the first-plan near late days of **45** but not the far late days of 90; and **100** otherwise, that is, at 45 days or fewer.

Under the first-plan member appeal, the contested charges are multiplied by the late-claim percent, divided by one hundred.

**Either side of the thresholds.** 91 days takes 85 percent and 90 days takes 95 percent; 46 days takes 95 percent and 45 days takes 100 percent.

**Hypothetical example.** An order collected on 2 February and a claim filed on 10 May of the same non-leap year: 97 calendar days, more than 90, so 85 percent. Contested charges of 300.00 USD multiplied by 85, divided by one hundred, give 255.00 USD.
